extracted.intended_audience: Florida agencies, regulated persons, attorneys, policy advocates, and members of the public seeking a plain-language summary of the Florida Administrative Procedure Act
extracted.subtask_description: A Ballotpedia wiki summary of Florida's Chapter 120 (Administrative Procedure Act) describing statutory definitions, rulemaking procedures, requirements for meetings/hearings, maintenance of final orders, standards for judicial review, variances/waivers, and related administrative processes. Useful as an overview for practitioners, regulated parties, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (agency, rule, final order, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory definitions used throughout the chapter, including "agency," "agency action," "agency head," "division," "final order," "invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority," "rule," "rulemaking authority," "variance," "waiver," "party," and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides precise scope of terms (e.g., what counts as an agency; what is a rule vs. internal memoranda; final order includes materials explicitly adopted). Many procedural rights and obligations turn on these definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed or existing rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority if any one of the following applies: (a) agency materially failed to follow applicable rulemaking procedures; (b) agency exceeded its grant of rulemaking authority; (c) rule enlarges, modifies, or contravenes the specific provisions of law implemented; (d) rule is vague, fails to establish adequate standards, or vests unbridled discretion; (e) rule is arbitrary or capricious; (f) rule imposes regulatory costs that could be reduced by less costly alternatives that substantially accomplish statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists substantive and procedural bases for challenging the validity of a rule; emphasizes both conformity to statutory authority and reasoned, cost-considerate rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking is required under statutory rules procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency statement defined as a rule shall be adopted by the rulemaking procedure provided by s.120.54 as soon as feasible and practicable; rulemaking is not a matter of agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes presumptions: rulemaking presumed feasible unless agency proves lack of time or unresolved related matters; presumed practicable to provide fair notice unless detail/precision unreasonable or issue too narrow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption standards for feasibility and practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking shall be presumed feasible unless the agency proves it has not had sufficient time to acquire knowledge/experience or related matters unresolved; practicable unless the agency proves precision/detail is unreasonable or matter is so narrow it is impractical outside adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These presumptions allocate burden to agencies to justify bypassing rulemaking in favor of other actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least-cost alternative requirement in rule adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: In adopting rules, agencies must, among alternative approaches to any regulatory objective and to the extent allowed by law, choose the alternative that does not impose regulatory costs on the regulated person, county, or city which could be reduced by adoption of less costly alternatives that substantially accomplish the statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates consideration of cost-minimizing alternatives that still achieve statutory objectives; ties back to invalid exercise grounds (costly alternatives may make rule vulnerable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-subject requirement for rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule adopted shall contain only one subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits scope and bundling of rule provisions to a single subject to aid notice and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference rules and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may incorporate material by reference only as the material exists on the adoption date. For rules adopted after Dec. 31, 2010, incorporated material must be submitted in prescribed electronic format and be publicly accessible via hyperlink from the rule, unless posting would violate federal copyright law (in which case location and inspection details must be provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: referencing another agency rule generally incorporates subsequent amendments unless contrary intent; a rule may not be amended by reference only — amendments must set out the amended rule in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and publication timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule published in the Florida Administrative Code must be indexed by the Department of State within 90 days after the rule is filed. Agencies must publish notices and certain materials within statutorily prescribed timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures timely public availability and indexing of new rules; Department of State sets additional procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation limits for agency head responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency head may delegate authority to initiate rule development, but certain rulemaking responsibilities (specified subsections) may not be delegated or transferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves decision accountability for core rulemaking responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule development notice and workshops requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall provide notice of the development of proposed rules by publication of a notice of rule development in the Florida Administrative Register before providing notice of a proposed rule; rule development may include workshops and negotiated rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide early public notice and opportunity for participation during development; agencies must follow formal notice steps before proposing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public meetings, hearings, and workshops notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for emergency meetings, agencies shall give notice of public meetings, hearings, and workshops by publication in the Florida Administrative Register and on the agency’s website not less than 7 days before the event; notice must include a statement of the general subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides minimum public notice period and required content of notices to ensure public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda availability and change limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An agenda shall be prepared so that a copy may be received at least 7 days before the event by any person in the state who requests a copy (and pays reasonable cost); meeting materials (electronic excluding confidential/exempt info) must be published on the agency website. After publication, agenda changes only for good cause as determined and stated in the record; notification of change must be at earliest practicable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects predictability of public meetings and access to materials; limits last-minute agenda changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency public meetings procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If immediate danger to public health, safety, or welfare requires immediate action, an agency may hold an emergency public meeting using any fair procedure necessary; the procedure must provide at least the procedural protection given by statutes/constitutions, the agency must limit action to necessary measures, and must publish written findings of facts/reasons for emergency and fairness — these findings are judicially reviewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows expedited action when necessary but requires contemporaneous justification and subjects that justification to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum rules for remote participation (regional planning councils)
rubrics_metrics.description: For regional planning councils covering three+ counties, a voting member appearing via telephone/real-time videoconferencing may be counted toward quorum if at least one-third of voting members are physically present and the remote member notifies intent to appear at least 24 hours before the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conditions under which remote participation counts toward quorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and electronic transmission of agency final orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must electronically transmit a certified text-searchable copy of each agency final order rendered on/after July 1, 2015, to a centralized electronic database maintained by the division; the database must permit full-text research by agency name, date, type, subject, and terms. Specified categories of final orders must be transmitted and others listed; transmission or listing generally within 90 days after final order rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements to attach complete text of materials incorporated by reference or state location and inspection method if impractical to attach; centralized database is official compilation for orders rendered on/after 7/1/2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of State coordination duties for final orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of State shall coordinate transmittal, indexing, management, preservation, and availability of agency final orders; provide guidelines for indexing, storage/retrieval systems, standards for certification and electronic transmittal, and security standards; determine which final orders must be indexed or transmitted and require agencies to report which orders establish precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department may approve more than one indexing/storage system and adopt binding rules to administer responsibilities; may designate an alternative official compiler if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking authority constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant of rulemaking authority is necessary but not sufficient; an agency may adopt only rules that implement or interpret specific powers and duties granted by the enabling statute. Statutory language granting general powers is construed no further than implementing or interpreting specific powers/duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits agencies from adopting rules merely because they are reasonably related to an enabling statute's purpose or are not arbitrary/capricious; limits rulemaking to implementation/interpretation of specific statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of statutory repeal on existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If provisions of law implemented by a rule are repealed: (a) a rule that on its face implements only the repealed provision is nullified; (b) a rule implementing both repealed and other provisions is nullified as to the repealed portions unless the agency publishes notice of rule development within 180 days otherwise the rule's operation is suspended; (c) repeal causing uncertain enforceability triggers treatment under s.120.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets mechanisms and timeframes for updating or suspending rules affected by legislative repeal and protects against enforcement of rules lacking statutory support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to repeal rules by committee or substantially affected persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Procedures Committee or any substantially affected person may petition an agency to repeal any rule (or portion) because it exceeds rulemaking authority. Agency must, within 30 days (if headed by individual) or 45 days (if collegial), initiate repeal proceedings or deny the petition with written reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides administrative remedy and timeline for affected persons to seek repeal of overbroad rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and incorporation of materials into rulemaking records
rubrics_metrics.description: In rulemaking proceedings, the agency may recognize materials judicially noticed and provide that those materials be incorporated into the record. Before the record is completed, all parties shall be provided a list of these materials and given reasonable opportunity to examine them and offer written comments or written rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency when agencies rely on external materials and allows parties to respond before the record is closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variances and waivers standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'variance' is a decision granting modification to all/part of a rule's literal requirements; a 'waiver' is a decision not to apply all/part of a rule to a person. Any variance or waiver shall conform to the standards outlined in the chapter and in uniform rules adopted pursuant to s.120.54(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes individualized relief from literal rule requirements but requires conformity with statutory/uniform criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk impact statement for health-based rules (DEP and Dept. of Agriculture)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Environmental Protection must prepare a risk impact statement for any rule proposed for approval by the Environmental Regulation Commission that establishes/changes standards or criteria based on impacts to human health; Dept. of Agriculture and Consumer Services must prepare a risk impact statement for any proposed rule establishing standards/criteria based on human health impacts. The statement must explain the risk addressed and identify/summarize scientific sources used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires publication of availability of a clear and concise risk impact statement; does not create new cause of action or diminish existing bases for challenge; certain federal identical rules are exempt but federal scientific information must be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and special requirements (specified subjects and entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter contains special exceptions and requirements for certain units (e.g., local governments with jurisdiction in one county, prisoners and parolees, regulation of professions regarding sexual misconduct proceedings, hunting and fishing regulation, school board special meeting agendas, students not considered persons for variances/waivers, specified education-related rule adoptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies limited categories where general chapter requirements are modified or do not apply; agencies and affected parties must consult the relevant subsection for applicability.
